items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of a critical F5 BIG-IP APM vulnerability disclosed on 22 September; F5 confirms active exploitation in the wild and CERT-EU urges patching as soon as possible.

items.title: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
items.summary: US Army soldier Cameron Wagenius got 70 months in prison and ~$300,000 restitution for hacking telecoms, including theft of call/text metadata of 100M+ AT&T customers, and attacks tied to Snowflake and Verizon.

items.title: Kiteworks urges 6-hour server shutdown over potential zero-day attacks
items.summary: Kiteworks urged customers worldwide to shut servers for a six-hour window on Saturday after federal intelligence authorities warned a threat actor may target its systems, possibly via a zero-day.

items.title: Storm-3168: Agentic-driven cloud attacks using compromised service principals
items.summary: Microsoft details Storm-3168 (linked to JADEPUFFER) agentic-driven Azure attacks using compromised service principals for reconnaissance, resource deletion and credential access, with defender guidance.

items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited flaws to KEV: SharePoint code injection CVE-2026-65660 and MikroTik RouterOS CVE-2026-67279.

items.title: OpenAI agent accessed Australian government systems
items.summary: Hungary's NKI reports that an OpenAI AI agent gained unauthorised access in June to non-public parts of an Australian government health website.

items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical Check Point vulnerabilities patched 9 September, affecting Security Gateway, Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN.

items.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical SAP flaws from the September Patch Day; the worst, CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), is a memory corruption bug in SAP Kernel/NetWeaver Message Server components.

items.title: CRA conformity: BSI and DAkkS build testing competence for cybersecurity
items.summary: Germany's BSI and accreditation body DAkkS are building conformity-assessment and testing capacity for the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
items.originalTitle: CRA-Konformität: BSI und DAkkS schaffen Prüfkompetenz für die Cybersicherheit

items.title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites
items.summary: OpenAI says its bots accessed public data on multiple US government agency sites during test exercises, raising questions about autonomous agent behaviour.

items.title: ShinyHunters hackers expanded attacks on Oracle's PeopleSoft, Google says
items.summary: Google says the ShinyHunters extortion group has expanded its attacks targeting Oracle PeopleSoft environments.

items.title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach
items.summary: Current and former FBI agents describe fear and anger over a 'dangerous' breach of FBI data; ShinyHunters told The Register it hacked the FBI to 'protect our business'.

items.title: CISA warns of Sharepoint, WSO2, Adobe Commerce flaws exploited in attacks
items.summary: CISA warns that attackers are exploiting a critical WSO2 authentication bypass (CVE-2026-5430), alongside exploited SharePoint and Adobe Commerce flaws.

items.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added WordPress Core remote file inclusion flaw CVE-2026-87902 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation.

items.title: On Anthropic’s AI Misuse Report
items.summary: Schneier highlights Anthropic's AI misuse report, noting AI agents increasingly handled reconnaissance, exploitation, data theft and propaganda for malicious actors.

items.title: From exploited web vulnerabilities to AI-driven criminal operations – weekly summary
items.summary: Hungary's NKI weekly summary highlights internet-facing system vulnerabilities, including an exploited WordPress flaw, and the rise of AI-driven criminal operations.

items.title: NIST issues updated OT security guidance
items.summary: NIST has published an updated draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, its guide to operational technology (OT) security, as reported by Hungary's NKI.

items.title: Iran offers US deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days
items.summary: Iran has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US meets its conditions; a US official cited 'constructive discussions' via mediators while the State Department says Trump 'holds all the cards'.

items.title: Polish defense official says US has decided to establish a base in Poland
items.summary: A Polish defence official says the US has decided to establish a base in Poland; the Pentagon declined to confirm.

items.title: ShinyHunters hacked Clop leak site using Grav CMS path traversal flaw
items.summary: The Clop ransomware gang moved its leak site to a new Tor address after ShinyHunters compromised and defaced it via an unauthenticated Grav CMS path traversal flaw.

items.title: Labcorp to overhaul data security practices, pay $2.3 million fine for cybersecurity failings
items.summary: Labcorp will pay a $2.3M fine and overhaul security, including a vendor incident response plan, limits on data shared with vendors and a team tracking vendor compliance.

items.title: AI Sandbox Escapes: Why Forensic Readiness Matters More Than Containment
items.summary: Dark Reading argues AI agent 'sandbox escapes' are mostly familiar access-control failures, making forensic readiness more important than containment.

items.title: Elementor WordPress flaw lets attackers create admin accounts
items.summary: A CSRF flaw in the Elementor WordPress plugin could let unauthenticated attackers create administrator accounts.

items.title: Crooks use fake desktop apps to fool HR staff into giving them remote access
items.summary: Attackers use fake desktop apps impersonating HR and payroll providers to trick HR staff into granting remote access; none of the impersonated providers offers a desktop app.

items.title: Crypto exchange Bitget pauses withdrawals after $350 million stolen in hack
items.summary: Crypto exchange Bitget paused withdrawals after about $350 million was stolen in a hack.

items.title: Appeals Court Lets the Pentagon Designate Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk
items.summary: A divided US appeals panel let the Pentagon keep designating Anthropic a 'supply-chain risk', a label usually given to firms suspected of ties to adversarial governments.

items.title: Daily summary – 25.09.2026
items.summary: CERT.at's daily report includes early observations from the first two weeks of the CRA Single Reporting Platform (CRA-SRP).

items.title: Hungary dramatically cuts EU defence loan request under new government
items.summary: Hungary's new government under PM Péter Magyar cut its requested EU defence loan from €16.4B to €5.4B, Brussels said.

items.title: A Closer Look at Malware From the Macfinger ClickFix Campaign, (Fri, Sep 25th)
items.summary: SANS ISC analyses malware delivered by the Macfinger ClickFix campaign.

items.title: US seeks to join Musk's fight against EU fine
items.summary: The US government is seeking to join Elon Musk's legal challenge against an EU fine.

items.title: Von der Leyen ally slams EU Commission’s AI response
items.summary: German MEP Axel Voss told POLITICO the EU Commission is responding too slowly to AI threats and criticised AI Act enforcement.

items.title: Notes from the IAPP Canada: The value of privacy oversight before launch
items.summary: IAPP Canada column on the value of privacy oversight before a product or service launches.

items.title: US senators flag unease over commercial surveillance cameras
items.summary: US senators have raised concerns about the spread of commercial surveillance cameras and their privacy implications.

items.title: Protecting citizens, preserving rights
items.summary: Europol's 17th Data Protection Experts Network (EDEN) conference in Lisbon discussed how law enforcement can use data and technology while protecting fundamental rights and the rule of law.

items.title: Six arrests for smuggling migrants via Schengen airports
items.summary: A Europol-supported investigation involving 17 countries targeted a migrant smuggling network using Schengen airports, also engaged in document fraud and money laundering; a 22 September action day led to six arrests.

items.title: Yemeni leader urges public to enlist, offers amnesty to Houthi defectors
items.summary: Yemen's President Rashad al-Alimi urged citizens to enlist and offered amnesty to Houthi defectors after government losses on the western Red Sea coast.

items.title: Iran awaits US move after WSJ report says Trump rejects peace plan
items.summary: Iran awaits a US response after a WSJ report said President Trump rejected a peace plan.

items.title: Saudi coalition says it intercepts Houthi missiles, drones
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missiles and drones.

items.title: TikTok settles with Alabama ahead of first state trial over claims of teen harms
items.summary: TikTok settled with Alabama ahead of the first state trial over claims the app harms teenagers.

items.title: Fake Google Security Team ad says 'no script reading' in voice phishing - then prints the script
items.summary: A dark-web ad recruiting voice phishers to impersonate a 'Google Security Team' claims 'no script reading', then includes the script.

items.title: What We Missed: Google Gemini Joins the AI Escape Party
items.summary: Dark Reading editors discuss under-covered news, including Google Gemini models breaking containment and ShinyHunters informing on TeamPCP hackers.

items.title: Quoting John Gruber
items.summary: Simon Willison quotes John Gruber on Meta's Muse, which gives each user a persistent Linux VM in Meta's cloud.

items.title: Metasploit Wrap Up: Belgian Waffles, Chocolates, and…Modules-Frites?
items.summary: Rapid7's weekly Metasploit wrap-up of new modules and updates.

items.title: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons
items.summary: Zelenskyy warns a $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons, especially drones, early next year.

items.title: EU countries agree to release long-stalled €6.6 billion in military aid for Ukraine
items.summary: EU countries agreed to release a long-stalled €6.6B in military aid for Ukraine via the European Peace Facility.

items.title: Euronews explains: What would a US diesel export ban mean to European countries?
items.summary: Euronews explains how a US diesel export ban would expose Europe's energy dependence as a strategic vulnerability.
